newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dyno Nobel says signs A$65 mln contract.
newsitem.headline: Dyno Nobel says signs A$65 mln contract.

text.p: Dyno Nobel, a subsidiary of Norway's Dyno Industrier ASA said on Thursday it had signed a six-year contract with Newmont Gold to supply explosives for a copper and gold mine in Indonesia.
The company, which has its Asia-Pacific headquarters in Sydney, said the contract with Newmont's Batu Hijau copper-gold project was worth more than A$65 million.
It said Newmont recently began development work on the project, on the island of Sumbawa, where mineral production is expected to begin at the end of the decade.
The first delivery of explosives will start later this month. Dyno will also provide ammonium nitrate and initiation systems and services, it said.
Phil Mitchell, general manager international for Dyno Nobel Asia-Pacific, said the deal entrenched the firm's position as the largest supplier of explosives in the fast-growing Indonesian market.
